oewn-14507501-n.learner: a chance to do something that is there because the circumstances happen to suit you
examples: I shall take the opportunity of calling in Grosvenor Street.
he readily engaged for taking the earliest opportunity of waiting on her after his return from London

oewn-01496967-v.learner: to put something in a place, either a real place or one you only think of
examples: He set the candle on the table beside the letter.
She set the box down at his feet.

oewn-00299677-v.learner: to make something be in a certain state
examples: A single spark set the dry hedge ablaze.
His kind words set her at ease.

oewn-00949109-v.learner: to decide on something and make it definite
examples: They set the date of the wedding for the first of May.

oewn-00159432-r.learner: used to show that something is exact, and nothing else
examples: Very true, my dear, that is exactly what I say.
that is exactly what I could most wish for

oewn-00370083-r.learner: in a way that is exact
examples: Upon my word, I cannot exactly explain the matter
She measured the cloth exactly before she cut it.

oewn-00370459-r.learner: in just the way it should be
examples: Everything went exactly as it should.
The two halves fitted together exactly.

oewn-01348685-v.learner: to make something open, or make it come open
examples: as he opened the door
the pianoforte was opened
The door opened slowly and a cold wind came in.

oewn-02431018-v.learner: to begin working, or to make something begin working
examples: A new shop opened on the corner last week.

oewn-00049115-n.learner: the act of coming to a place
examples: Four weeks were to pass away before her uncle and aunt's arrival.
The housekeeper at Netherfield had received orders to prepare for the arrival of her master

oewn-09829571-n.learner: a person who arrives, or who has arrived
examples: The new arrivals were shown up to their rooms.

oewn-00048966-n.learner: the reaching of something you were aiming at
examples: Their arrival at an agreement took the whole afternoon.

oewn-00061741-r.learner: at a time that comes after the time being talked about
examples: When alone with Elizabeth afterwards, she spoke more on the subject.
Mrs. Bennet was satisfied, and soon afterwards ordered her carriage.

oewn-00633399-v.learner: to expect something, or to believe or suppose that it is so
examples: the sort of cautiousness to which you, I imagine, have been alluding
don't imagine it was from any silly cause

oewn-01639939-v.learner: to form a picture in your mind of something that is not there, or that is not the case
examples: Who could have imagined that we should receive an invitation to dine there
She shut her eyes and imagined the sea.

oewn-00773677-v.learner: to make someone do a certain thing
examples: it led him to escape out of Longbourn House the next morning with admirable slyness
which lead me to perform what I look on as a point of duty

oewn-02003455-v.learner: to travel in front of other people; to go ahead of them
examples: Colonel Fitzwilliam, who led the way, was about thirty

oewn-02003830-v.learner: to take someone to a place
examples: He took her hand and led her into the garden.

oewn-00149403-v.learner: to come to be in a certain state or condition
examples: His complexion became pale with anger
She became jealous of his esteem, when she could no longer hope to be benefited by it.

oewn-02632685-v.learner: to go through a change and turn into something else
examples: she was herself becoming an object of some interest in the eyes of his friend
In those years a new nation became.

oewn-13952621-n.learner: the state of being with another person
examples: Mr. Collins, to be sure, was neither sensible nor agreeable: his society was irksome
It could not be for society, as he frequently sat there ten minutes together without opening his lips

oewn-07982754-n.learner: a large group of people living together with their own way of life and their own way of running things
examples: I consider it as one of the first refinements of polished societies.

oewn-08244135-n.learner: an organized group of people who join together because they share an interest
examples: She joined a society for the study of old books.
